accepted.claim: Applicants for a Student Pass in higher education must be outside Malaysia when submitting the application.
accepted.action: Ensure you are physically outside Malaysia before submitting your Student Pass application.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Applicants MUST BE OUTSIDE MALAYSIA at the time of application submission.

accepted.claim: International students arriving in Malaysia must undergo a Post-Arrival Medical Examination within 7 days of entry.
accepted.action: Schedule and complete your Post-Arrival Medical Examination within 7 days of arriving in Malaysia.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Upon arrival in Malaysia, students must undergo a Post-Arrival Medical Examination within 7 days.

accepted.claim: Student Pass holders from Public Universities or Private Higher Education Institutions may work part-time for up to 20 hours per week.
accepted.action: Limit your part-time work to 20 hours per week and only at approved locations if you hold a Student Pass from a UA or IPTS.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Student Pass holders are allowed to work part-time during their study period, limited to 20 hours per week, only at approved locations:

accepted.claim: Part-time work for international students is restricted to specific approved locations such as restaurants, petrol stations, mini markets, hotels, and university/college areas.
accepted.action: Ensure any part-time job you accept is located in an approved venue such as a restaurant, petrol station, mini market, hotel, or university/college area.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Student Pass holders are allowed to work part-time during their study period, limited to 20 hours per week, only at approved locations: Restaurants Petrol stations Mini markets Hotels University/college areas

accepted.claim: International students are prohibited from performing front desk duties or working as student recruitment agents.
accepted.action: Do not accept jobs involving front desk duties or student recruitment, as these are prohibited.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Students are prohibited from front desk duties in line with current foreign worker policies and from working as student recruitment agents.

accepted.claim: Applying for Student Pass work permission requires submitting a job offer letter and a support letter from the institution.
accepted.action: Collect a job offer letter and an institutional support letter stating work permission request, semester schedule, and holiday dates for your work permission application.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Applications must be submitted to the Student Pass Unit, Immigration Department HQ/State Immigration Office with the following documents: Job offer letter Support letter from the institution (UA/IPTS) stating work permission request, semester schedule, and holiday dates

accepted.claim: The cost for a Student Pass application is RM60.00.
accepted.action: Budget RM60.00 for the Student Pass application fee.

accepted.claim: The cost for a Social Visit Pass for dependents or guardians is RM90.00.
accepted.action: Budget RM90.00 for any Social Visit Pass application for dependents or guardians.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Social Visit Pass for Dependents / Guardians of Student Pass holders – RM90.00

accepted.claim: Students must have a passport valid for at least 18 months when applying for a Student Pass.
accepted.action: Verify that your passport validity is at least 18 months from the time of application.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Copy of passport (all pages including cover; validity must be at least 18 months)

accepted.claim: Students must possess a health insurance policy recognized in Malaysia with a coverage period of at least 12 months.
accepted.action: Purchase a health insurance policy recognized in Malaysia that covers you for at least 12 months.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Health Insurance Policy recognized in Malaysia with a coverage period of at least 12 months.

accepted.claim: Only Student Pass holders at Master’s or PhD level are permitted to bring dependents to reside in Malaysia.
accepted.action: If you wish to bring dependents, ensure you are enrolled in a Master’s or PhD program.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Only Student Pass holders at Master’s or PhD level are permitted to bring dependents to reside in Malaysia.

accepted.claim: Dependents of international students are not allowed to work, conduct business, or engage in political activities.
accepted.action: Inform your dependents that they are prohibited from working, conducting business, or engaging in political activities in Malaysia.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Dependents are NOT ALLOWED to work, conduct business, deliver political speeches, lectures, or engage in political activities.

accepted.claim: eVISA applications for a Single Entry Visa can be made worldwide except from Malaysia, Israel, and North Korea.
accepted.action: If you need a Single Entry Visa, apply via the eVISA portal from a location that is not Malaysia, Israel, or North Korea.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Note: eVISA applications can be made worldwide, except from Malaysia, Israel, and North Korea

accepted.claim: Violation of Student Pass regulations can result in the revocation of the pass.
accepted.action: Comply strictly with all Student Pass regulations to avoid having your pass revoked.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Any student found violating regulations will have their Student Pass revoked.

accepted.claim: Translations of documents from the country of origin must be certified by foreign missions or embassies in Malaysia.
accepted.action: Ensure all document translations from your home country are certified by the relevant foreign mission or embassy in Malaysia.
accepted.evidenceQuote: Translations from the country of origin must be certified by foreign missions/embassies in Malaysia.
